content: 1. Budesonide reduces the effects of rosiglitazone through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This interaction is considered minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. Caution and monitoring are advised. 2. Budesonide decreases the efficacy of the live rotavirus oral vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This interaction is serious, and alternative therapies should be used. Corticosteroids, including budesonide, increase the risk of infection when co-administered with live vaccines. 3. Rucaparib increases the levels or effects of budesonide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism in the liver and intestines. Close monitoring is required, and dosage adjustments of CYP3A4 substrates may be necessary. 4. Rufinamide decreases the levels or effects of budesonide by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 5. Co-administration of budesonide and non-ASA salicylates may increase the toxicity of either drug due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Budesonide also reduces salicylate levels by enhancing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, and caution is advised. 6. Budesonide and salsalate may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism. Budesonide also reduces salsalate levels by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, and close monitoring is recommended. 7. Sarecycline increases the levels or effects of budesonide by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring for toxicities are advised, and dosage reductions of P-gp substrates may be necessary. 8. Budesonide enhances the effects of sargramostim through pharmacodynamic synergism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 9. Budesonide decreases the levels or effects of saxagliptin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 10. Budesonide reduces the levels or effects of silodosin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative therapies should be considered. 11. Simvastatin increases the levels or effects of budesonide by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 12. Budesonide decreases the efficacy of sipuleucel-T through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 13. Sirolimus increases the levels or effects of budesonide by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Budesonide also reduces the levels or effects of sirolimus by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative therapies should be used. 14. Budesonide reduces the effects of sitagliptin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 15. Budesonide decreases the efficacy of live smallpox and mpox (vaccinia) vaccines through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This interaction is contraindicated, as corticosteroids increase the risk of infection with live vaccines. 16. Budesonide and a combination of sodium sulfate, potassium chloride, magnesium sulfate, and polyethylene glycol both reduce serum potassium levels. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 17. Budesonide reduces the levels or effects of solifenacin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 18. Budesonide decreases the effects of somatrem through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 19. Budesonide reduces the effects of somatropin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 20. Budesonide decreases the levels of sorafenib by increasing its metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 21. Sotorasib reduces the levels or effects of budesonide by inducing the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. This interaction is serious, and alternative therapies should be used. If unavoidable, refer to the prescribing information for dosage adjustments. 22. Budesonide increases the toxicity of squill through an unspecified mechanism. This interaction is serious, and alternative therapies should be used. 23. St. John’s Wort reduces the levels or effects of budesonide by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. This interaction is serious, and alternative therapies should be used. 24. Stiripentol increases the levels or effects of budesonide by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Consider reducing the dose of P-gp substrates if adverse reactions occur. 25. Budesonide reduces the levels or effects of sufentanil by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 26. Budesonide and sulfasalazine may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism. Budesonide also reduces sulfasalazine levels by enhancing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, and caution is advised. 27. Budesonide and sulindac may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, with an increased risk of gastrointestinal ulceration. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 28. Budesonide reduces the levels or effects of sunitinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 29. Budesonide reduces the levels or effects of tacrolimus by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, while tacrolimus increases the levels or effects of budesonide by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 30. Budesonide reduces the levels or effects of tadalafil by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 31. Tecovirimat reduces the levels or effects of budesonide by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Tecovirimat is a weak CYP3A4 inducer, and close monitoring of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates is recommended. 32. Budesonide reduces the levels or effects of temsirolimus by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 33. Tepotinib increases the levels or effects of budesonide by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. This interaction is serious, and alternative therapies should be used. If unavoidable, reduce the P-gp substrate dosage as recommended. 34. Budesonide and testosterone may enhance each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergism, potentially increasing edema formation. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 35. Budesonide reduces the efficacy of tetanus toxoid vaccines through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This interaction is contraindicated, as corticosteroids increase the risk of infection with live vaccines. 36. Budesonide reduces the levels or effects of theophylline by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 37. Budesonide decreases the efficacy of tick-borne encephalitis vaccines through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This interaction is contraindicated, as corticosteroids increase the risk of infection with live vaccines. 38. Budesonide reduces the levels or effects of tipranavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 39. Budesonide and tolfenamic acid may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, with an increased risk of gastrointestinal ulceration. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 40. Budesonide and tolmetin may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, with an increased risk of gastrointestinal ulceration. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 41. Budesonide reduces the levels or effects of tolterodine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 42. Tolvaptan increases the levels or effects of budesonide by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter, while budesonide reduces the levels or effects of tolvaptan by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative therapies should be used. 43. Topiramate reduces the levels or effects of budesonide by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 44. Budesonide and torsemide may increase the risk of hypokalemia through pharmacodynamic synergism, especially with strong glucocorticoid activity. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 45. Tovorafenib reduces the levels or effects of budesonide by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative therapies should be used. If unavoidable, monitor for loss of efficacy. 46. Budesonide and trastuzumab may increase each other's toxicity through immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 47. Budesonide decreases the efficacy of inactivated travelers' diarrhea and cholera vaccines through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This interaction is contraindicated, as corticosteroids increase the risk of infection with live vaccines. 48. Budesonide reduces the levels or effects of trazodone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, while trazodone reduces the levels or effects of budesonide by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 49. Budesonide reduces the levels or effects of triamcinolone acetonide injectable suspension by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 50. Budesonide reduces the levels or effects of triazolam by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 51. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of budesonide by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative therapies should be used. 52. Budesonide decreases the efficacy of typhoid polysaccharide and live vaccines through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This interaction is contraindicated, as corticosteroids increase the risk of infection with live vaccines. 53. Budesonide reduces the levels or effects of vardenafil by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 54. Budesonide decreases the efficacy of the live varicella virus vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This interaction is contraindicated, as corticosteroids increase the risk of infection with live vaccines. 55. Verapamil increases the levels or effects of budesonide by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and CYP3A4 metabolism. Budesonide also reduces the levels or effects of verapamil by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 56. Budesonide reduces the effects of vildagliptin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 57. Budesonide reduces the levels or effects of vincristine liposomal by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 58. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of budesonide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 59. Budesonide reduces the levels of willow bark by enhancing renal clearance. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 60. Budesonide and xipamide may increase the risk of hypokalemia through pharmacodynamic synergism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 61. Budesonide decreases the efficacy of the yellow fever vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This interaction is contraindicated, as corticosteroids increase the risk of infection with live vaccines. 62. Zafirlukast increases the levels or effects of budesonide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 63. Budesonide reduces the levels or effects of ziprasidone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 64. Budesonide reduces the levels or effects of zonisamide by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 65. Budesonide decreases the efficacy of the live zoster vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This interaction is contraindicated, as corticosteroids increase the risk of infection with live vaccines. 66. Budesonide reduces the efficacy of the recombinant zoster vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Immunosuppressive therapies may reduce the effectiveness of the recombinant zoster vaccine.
